rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says he would not have shared anything had God not bound the People of Scripture by this covenant, then he recited the verse.
rows.anchor: لولا ما أخذ الله على أهل الكتاب ما حدثتكم بشيء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that whoever conceals knowledge from those who need it will be bridled with fire on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: من كتم علما عن أهله ألجم يوم القيامة لجاما من نار

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says God required scholars to teach before requiring the ignorant to learn; al-Zuhri then agreed to narrate forty reports.
rows.anchor: ما أخذ الله على أهل الجهل أن يتعلموا حتى أخذ على أهل العلم أن يعلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humayd ibn Kathir, Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, and Abu ʿAmr read the verb in the third person with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأه حميد بن كثير وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readers use the second-person t-reader; on this reading Muhammad is addressed and told not to think the rejoicers escape punishment.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فمعناه: ولا تحسبن يا محمد الفارحين بمفازة من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the third-person reading, the rejoicers themselves must not suppose their joy will save them from punishment.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأه بالياء فمعناه: ولا يحسبن الفارحون منجيا لهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The t-reading with fatḥa on the bāʾ is a renewed emphasis.
rows.anchor: لا تحسبن بالتاء، وفتح الباء إعادة تأكيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك وعيسى
rows.claim: They read the second-person form with ḍamma on bāʾ, addressing Muhammad and his companions.
rows.anchor: بالتاء وضم الباء، أراد محمدا وأصحابه

rows.speaker: محمد وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: They read the third-person form with ḍamma on bāʾ, reporting that the rejoicers should not suppose this about themselves.
rows.anchor: وقرأ محمد وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويحيى بن يعمر: بالياء وضم الباء

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار عن أبي سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Some hypocrites promised to campaign with the Prophet, stayed behind, then rejoiced and sought praise for deeds they had not done.
rows.anchor: عطاء بن يسار عن أبي سعيد الخدري: أن رجالا من المنافقين

rows.speaker: رافع بن خديج
rows.claim: Rafiʿ says the verse concerns hypocrites who stayed behind on the Prophet’s journeys; Zayd confirms Rafiʿ’s account before Marwan.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم عن رافع بن خديج: أنه كان هو وزيد بن ثابت

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The verse concerns the Jewish scholars Finhas, Ashyaʿ, and their peers, who took pride in misleading people and being called learned.
rows.anchor: نزلت في فنحاص وأشيع وأشباههما من الأحبار، يفرحون بإضلالهم الناس

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: Jews in Medina wrote to Jews elsewhere to deny Muhammad’s prophethood, then rejoiced at their agreement to reject him and the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: هم يهود أهل المدينة كتبوا إلى يهود اليمن والشام وأطراف الأرض: أن محمدا ليس برسول

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Jews rejoiced that people admired their alteration of the Scripture.
rows.anchor: هم اليهود فرحوا بإعجاب الناس تبديلهم الكتاب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says Jews rejoiced over what God had given Abraham, although they had no share in it.
rows.anchor: هم اليهود فرحوا بما أعطى الله إبراهيم وهم براء من ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse concerns Jews who hid the answer to the Prophet’s question, misled him, and sought his praise for answering.
rows.anchor: إنما دعاء رسول الله اليهود فسألهم عن شيء فكتموه إياه وأخبروه بغيره

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Jews at Khaybar falsely professed belief and support; Muslims praised them, and they rejoiced at being praised for what they had not done.
rows.anchor: قتادة ومقاتل: أتت يهود خيبر

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim reports that some Jews equipped and funded an army against the Prophet; he read the verb for what they were given with a lengthened vowel.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ناس من اليهود جهزوا جيشا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنفقوا عليهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses the verb as meaning that the people were given something.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير أوتوا أي أعطوا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha recounts the Prophet’s tearful night prayer and his answer that he should be a grateful servant; he said the verse had been revealed that night and warned readers who fail to reflect.
rows.anchor: وما لي لا أبكي وقد أنزل الله تعالى في هذه الليلة علي إن في خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي عن أبيه
rows.claim: The Prophet would use the toothstick at night, look to the sky, and recite the passage through the plea to be protected from the Fire.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قام من الليل يسوك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة عن أبيه
rows.claim: The Prophet called this passage the most severe verse of the Qurʾan for the jinn.
rows.anchor: أشد آية في القرآن على الجن إن في خلق السماوات والأرض الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After learning of Moses’ and Jesus’ signs, Quraysh asked the Prophet to turn al-Safa into gold; this verse was revealed instead.
rows.anchor: فأتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس والنخعي وقتادة
rows.claim: They interpret remembering God standing, sitting, and lying down as prayer, with sitting and side-lying allowed when one cannot stand.
rows.anchor: هذا في الصلاة يصلي قائما، فإن لم يستطع فقاعدا فإن لم يستطع فعلى جنبه

rows.speaker: سائر المفسرين
rows.claim: Other commentators take the three states as constant remembrance, since people rarely leave all three states of being.
rows.anchor: أراد به ذكر الله تعالى، ووصفهم بالمداومة عليه، إذ الإنسان قلما يخلوا

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever wants to graze in the gardens of Paradise should remember God often.
rows.anchor: من أراد أن يرتع في رياض الجنة فليكثر ذكر الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report calls remembrance knowledge of faith, a cure for hypocrisy, and protection from Satan and the Fire.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى علم الإيمان وبرء من النفاق وحصن من الشيطان وحرز من النيران

rows.speaker: الله تعالى لموسى
rows.claim: God tells Moses to keep Him in mind, not forget His remembrance in any state, and make remembrance his concern.
rows.anchor: يا موسى اجعلني منك على بال ولا تنس ذكري على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on the heavens and earth shows that they have a powerful, wise maker and governor.
rows.anchor: إن لها صانعا قادرا ومدبرا حكيما

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: On the heavenly ascent, Gabriel says devils obscure human sight so people will not contemplate the heavens; otherwise they would see wonders.
rows.anchor: هذه الشياطين يحرقون على أعين بني آدم أن لا يتفكروا في ملكوت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عور
rows.claim: Thought dispels heedlessness and brings awe to the heart; grief and reflection polish and illuminate hearts, as water nourishes plants.
rows.anchor: الفكرة تذهب الغفلة وتحدث للقلب الخشية، كما يحدث الماء الزرع والنبات

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan was overcome after looking at the stars following prayer and was said to urinate blood from prolonged grief and reflection.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى الكواكب غشي عليه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A man contemplated the stars, affirmed that he had a Lord and creator, asked forgiveness, and God forgave him.
rows.anchor: أشهد أن لي ربا وخالقا اللهم اغفر لي فنظر الله إليه فغفر له

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: An Israelite worshipper’s father said his lack of a cloud was due to looking at the sky without reflection; creation was made for a great purpose, not in vain.
rows.anchor: هل رفعت طرفك إلى السماء ثم رددته بغير فكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fahisha means adultery; the text in ʿAbd Allah’s codex adds ‘of your women.’ Four Muslim witnesses establish the act.
rows.anchor: يعني الزنا، وفي مصحف عبد الله الفاحشة من نسائكم فاستشهدوا عليهن أربعة منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the prescribed punishments were revealed, women who committed adultery were confined at home until death or until God provided another rule.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان هذا قبل نزول الحدود، كانت المرأة في أول الإسلام لو أذنبت حبست في البيت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet announces the replacement penalty: one hundred lashes and stoning for a previously married adulterer, and one hundred lashes plus a year’s exile for a virgin.
rows.anchor: الثيب بالثيب جلد مائة ورجم بالحجارة، والبكر بالبكر جلد مائة وتغريب عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The confinement rule was abrogated by the later penalty, while the requirement for witnesses remained operative.
rows.anchor: وهو الإمساك في البيوت وبقي بعضها محكما وهو الاستشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired offenders are a man and woman; when masculine and feminine forms are paired, the masculine form is used, and the pronoun refers to al-fahisha.
rows.anchor: يعني الرجل والمرأة، المذكر والمؤنث إذا اجتمعا قلب المذكر على المؤنث

rows.speaker: عطاء وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: They say offenders should be rebuked verbally and reproached for not fearing God or being ashamed of adultery.
rows.anchor: يعني عيروهما وعنفوهما باللسان: أما خفت الله أما استحيت الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the offenders should be insulted and cursed.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: سبوهما واشتموهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas includes both verbal reproach and physical punishment with a hand or sandals.
rows.anchor: هو باللسان واليد كأن [يوذي] بالتعيير والضرب بالنعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the offenders repent and reform, they must no longer be harmed; the rule and the confinement rule were later replaced by the prescribed penalties.
rows.anchor: فلما نزلت الحدود نسخت هذه الآية والإمساك من الآية الأولى بالرجم للبنت والجلد والنفي للبكر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In the case of an illicit affair between a worker and his employer’s wife, the Prophet ordered one hundred lashes and a year’s exile for the son, and stoning for the woman after she confessed.
rows.anchor: أما غنمك وجاريتك فرد عليك، وجلد ابنك مائة وتغريبه عاما

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar applied exile as a penalty for fornication, and Marwan continued the practice in his governorship.
rows.anchor: أن عمر بن الخطاب (رضي الله عنه) غرب في الزنا ولم تزل تلك السنة حتى غرب مروان

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A man from Aslam confessed four times; after the Prophet verified he was sane and married, he ordered him stoned, and pursued him when he fled.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا من أسلم جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاعترف عنده بالزنا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines sinning in ignorance as choosing a fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure, paralleling the wording in al-Anʿam.
rows.anchor: معنى قوله: بجهالة اختيارهم اللذة الفانية على اللذة الباقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repenting ‘soon’ means before the sinner’s good deeds cancel the sin.
rows.anchor: ثم يتوبون من قريب معناه قبل أن يحبطون السوء بحسناته فيحبطها

rows.speaker: السدي والكلبي
rows.claim: They define ‘soon’ as repentance while still healthy, before illness or death.
rows.anchor: القريب ما دام في صحته قبل المرض والموت

rows.speaker: عكرمة وابن زيد
rows.claim: They say any repentance before death counts as soon.
rows.anchor: عكرمة وابن زيد: ما قبل الموت فهو قريب

rows.speaker: أبو مجلن والضحاك
rows.claim: They define the deadline as before the person sees the Angel of Death.
rows.anchor: قبل معاينة ملك الموت

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa gives the strikingly brief limit of a single camel’s pause before death.
rows.anchor: هو أن يتوب قبل موته بفواق ناقة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم عن عبد الرحمن السلماني
rows.claim: Four Companions successively report that repentance is accepted as late as a day, half-day, morning, and finally until the death rattle.
rows.anchor: إن الله عز وجل يقبل توبة العبد ما لم يغرغر بنفسه

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: The Prophet says acceptance extends from a year before death down to an hour and finally until the soul rattles in the throat.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من تاب قبل موته بسنة تاب الله عليه»

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In a report from al-Hasan, Iblis vows to tempt people until death, while God promises not to bar repentance before the death rattle.
rows.anchor: لا أحجب التوبة عن عبدي حتى يغرغر

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet reports Satan’s vow to mislead people while alive and God’s promise to keep forgiving those who seek His forgiveness.
rows.anchor: لا أزال أغفر لهم ما استغفروا لي

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Umar sought Ali’s daughter Umm Kulthum and cited the Prophet’s statement that every lineage and affinity ends except his; Ali married her to Umar for forty thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: إن كل نسب وصهر ينقطع يوم القيامة إلا نسبي وصهري

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Al-Hasan sent his new wife one hundred maidservants, each carrying one thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: إن الحسن (رضي الله عنه) تزوج بامرأة، فبعث إليها بمائة جارية

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
rows.claim: The Prophet says the best marriage is easiest; a man married without setting a dowry and later gave his Khaybar share, which his wife sold for one hundred thousand.
rows.anchor: خير النكاح أيسره

rows.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
rows.claim: A Companion who had not fixed a dowry before consummation assigned his wife his Khaybar share as her dowry when dying.
rows.anchor: إني قد أعطيتها من صداقها سهمي بخيبر

rows.speaker: النجاشي
rows.claim: The Prophet married Umm Habiba while she was in Abyssinia, and the Negus paid four hundred dinars as her dowry.
rows.anchor: وأن رسول الله زوجها فأصدق عنه النجاشي أربعمائة دينار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have married Salima al-Sulamiyya for ten thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: عن ابن سيرين عن ابن عباس أنه تزوج سليمة السلمية على عشرة آلاف درهم

rows.speaker: عروة البارقي
rows.claim: Urwa al-Bariqi married the daughter of Hani ibn Qabisa for one thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: أن عروة البارقي تزوج بنت هاني بن قبيصة على ألف درهم

rows.speaker: غيلان بن جرير
rows.claim: Ghilan ibn Jarir reports that Mutarrif paid ten thousand awqiya for his wife.
rows.anchor: أن مطرفا تزوج امرأة على عشرة ألف أواق

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar urged people not to inflate women’s dowries: the Prophet gave no wife or daughter more than twelve awqiya and warned that excessive payment could breed resentment.
rows.anchor: ألا لا تغالوا في صداق النساء، فإنها لو كانت مكرمة في الدنيا أو تقوى عند الله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The Prophet says a woman’s good fortune includes an easy dowry and an easy delivery.
rows.anchor: من يمن المرأة تيسير صداقها وتيسر رحمها

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Urwa adds his own view that one sign of ill fortune is an inflated dowry.
rows.anchor: وأنا أقول من عندي من أول شؤمها أن يكثر صداقها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says their customary dowry in the Prophet’s time was ten awqiya, which the text equates to four dirhams.
rows.anchor: كان صداقنا مذ كان فينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشرة أواق

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: The Prophet blessed ʿAbd al-Rahman after learning he married for a gold nugget’s weight and told him to hold a feast, even if with a sheep.
rows.anchor: تزوجت امرأة على وزن نواة من ذهب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported weight of the gold nugget is five dirhams.
rows.anchor: يقال: هي خمسة دراهم

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
rows.claim: A poor suitor had only his wrap, then no ring or goods, so the Prophet married him to the woman in exchange for what he knew of the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: زوجتك بما معك من القرآن

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عامر عن أبيه
rows.claim: A man offered two sandals as a dowry; the Prophet asked if the woman accepted and then approved the marriage.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أرضيت مالك بهاتين النعلين؟»

rows.speaker: أبو حدرد الأسلمي
rows.claim: When Abu Hadard asked for help with a two-hundred-dirham dowry, the Prophet quipped that even drawing water from Bathan would not yield more.
rows.anchor: قلت: مائتي درهم. فقال: «لو كنتم تغرفون من بطحان ما زدتم»

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: The Prophet says a man may make a marriage lawful by giving the woman two handfuls of sawiq or dates.
rows.anchor: من أعطى في صداق ملء كفيه سويقا أو تمرا فقد استحل

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet married a woman for ten dirhams.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تزوج بامرأة على عشرة دراهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib married his daughter for two dirhams.
rows.anchor: أن سعيد بن المسيب زوج ابنته على درهمين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says that a marriage made lawful for a single dirham is valid; Wakiʿ specifies that the statement concerns marriage.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من استحل بدرهم فقد استحل» قال وكيع: في النكاح

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid disallowed giving away a concubine by gift after the Prophet’s time, but says even a riding crop may serve as a valid dowry.
rows.anchor: إن الهبة لم تجز لأحد بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولو أصدقها سوطا لحلت

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim calls a ratl of silver the customary dowry, disapproves one or two dirhams as resembling prostitutes’ payments, and prefers twenty dirhams for free women.
rows.anchor: السنة في الصداق الرطل من الورق، كانوا يكرهون أن يكون مهر الحرائر مثل مهور البغايا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses those warned as people who fear being gathered, raised, and brought back to their Lord; another view says they know this will happen.
rows.anchor: الذين يخافون أن يحشروا يبعثوا ويحيوا إلى ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God there is no protector to benefit them or intercessor to speak for them, so they may become God-fearing.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم من دونه من دون الله ولي يعني قريب ينفعهم ولا شفيع يشفع لهم

rows.speaker: سليمان وخباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Suleiman and Khabbab say the command not to dismiss the worshippers was revealed about them.
rows.anchor: خباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna looked down on the poorly dressed believers and asked the Prophet to seat them elsewhere; he refused to expel believers.
rows.anchor: فلما رأوهم حوله حقروهم فأتوه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet refused the request to remove the believers, and Gabriel interrupted the attempt to write an agreement by revealing the prohibition.
rows.anchor: ما أنا بطارد المؤمنين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet stayed with the poor believers, sitting close and waiting for them rather than leaving them behind.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي لم يمتني حتى أمرني أن أصبر نفسي مع قوم من أمتي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the chiefs proposed separate days or one shared assembly where the Prophet would face them and turn his back to the poor; God forbade it.
rows.anchor: قالوا له: اجعل لنا يوما ولهم يوم، قال: لا أفعل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Quraysh scorned the poor followers and promised to follow Muhammad if he expelled them; they specifically named Bilal and Ibn Umm ʿAbd.
rows.anchor: أرضيت بهؤلاء من قومك؟ أفنحن نكون تبعا لهؤلاء

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: After leading Quraysh appealed through Abu Talib to expel poor adherents, Umar suggested testing what the chiefs wanted; the verse followed and Umar apologized.
rows.anchor: لو فعلت ذلك حتى ننظر ما الذي يريدون وإلى ما يصيرون فنزلت من قولهم هذه الآية

rows.speaker: جبير بن نفيل
rows.claim: Quraysh called the poor believers riffraff and asked that they be removed so Quraysh could become the Prophet’s companions.
rows.anchor: أرسلت إلينا فاطرد هؤلاء السقاط عنك فنكون أصحابك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the worshippers are poor people who prayed the obligatory dawn and afternoon prayers; nobles sought to displace them in the prayer line.
rows.anchor: يدعون ربهم يعني يعبدون ربهم بالصلاة المكتوبة بالغداة والعشي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains that the believers to be kept close are those who preserve congregational prayer.
rows.anchor: لا ولكنهم المحافظون على الصلوات في الجماعة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid tells Mujahid that the verse refers to people at prayer, not those rushing to a storyteller after morning prayer.
rows.anchor: إنما ذلك في الصلاة التي انصرفا عنها الآن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes the verse to support attending a remembrance gathering after the dawn prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: صليت الصبح مع سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says they recite the Qurʾan seeking God’s countenance; the clause about accountability answers the objection, and the prohibition clause governs the consequence.
rows.anchor: يعني يقرءون القرآن يريدون وجهه جواب لقوله ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says some nobles refused Islam after seeing a low-status person accept it first, out of pride at being preceded.
rows.anchor: كان الشريف إذا نظر إلى الوضيع قد آمن قبله حمى أنفا أن يسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ‘Has God favored these among us?’ is answered by saying God knows best who is grateful for Islam and deserves guidance.
rows.anchor: أليس الله بأعلم بالشاكرين يعني المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet sat among destitute migrants listening to Qurʾan and promised that the poor would enter Paradise half a day—five hundred years—before wealthy believers.
rows.anchor: تدخلون الجنة قبل أغنياء المؤمنين بنصف يوم مقداره خمس مائة سنة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: The Prophet says God approved his example of sitting with poor believers and calls their assembly a gathering of earlier prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: إن الله رضي لي أن أتأسى بمجالسكم وأن الله معنا

rows.speaker: عائذ بن عمرو
rows.claim: After Abu Bakr rebuked Salman, Suhayb, and Bilal for insulting Abu Sufyan, the Prophet warned that upsetting them upsets God; they forgave Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: لعلك أغضبتهم إن كنت أغضبتهم فقد أغضبت ربك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The welcome for those who believe in God’s signs concerns the poor whom God had forbidden the Prophet to dismiss; he would greet them first.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الذين نهى الله عز وجل نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم عن طردهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed when Umar apologized for advising the Prophet to accommodate the nobles’ request.
rows.anchor: جاء عمر (رضي الله عنه) للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاعتذر إليه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta names a broad group of early believers—including Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Bilal, Salman, Suhayb, and others—as its occasion.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وبلال وسالم وأبي عبيدة وصهيب

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Men confessed serious sins, the Prophet was silent, and the verse promising mercy and forgiveness was then revealed to them.
rows.anchor: إنا أصبنا ذنوبنا كثيرة عظيمة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains acting ‘in ignorance’ as not knowing what is lawful and forbidden; he also says every sinner is ignorant or unaware of the sin’s consequences.
rows.anchor: لا يعلم حلالا من حرام ومن جهالته ربك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ on the hamza in the two occurrences of innahu: Kufans open both; Ibn Kathir, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Umar, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi take them as resumptive; Hasan, Asim, and Yaʿqub use the first as an apposition, while Medina opens the first and breaks the second.
rows.anchor: واختلف القراء في قوله تعالى أنه [الكوفيون] بفتح الألف منهما جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguishes and explains the proofs and arguments against deniers and people of falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي نميز ونبين لك حجتنا وأدلتنا في كل من ينكر أهل الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The route of the criminals is to become clear; sabīl is masculine in Tamim and feminine in Hijaz, as other Qurʾanic usages show.
rows.anchor: والسبيل يذكر ويؤنث، فتميم تذكر، وأهل الحجاز يؤنثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘so that the path may be clear’ is read with either yāʾ or tāʾ; the Medinan reading uses tāʾ and accusative sabīl to address Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قرأ ولتستبين بالياء والتاء، وقرأ أهل المدينة ولتستبين بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is forbidden to worship the idols invoked by others and to follow their desires; expelling Bilal and Salman would have been a departure from guidance.
rows.anchor: قل لا أتبع أهواءكم في عبادة الأوثان وطرد بلال وسلمان قد ضللت

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: They read ḍalalt with kasra on the lām; the author says both verb patterns occur but the first is more correct and eloquent as Hijazi usage.
rows.anchor: قد ضللت، بكسر اللام وهما لغتان ضل يضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina means a clear explanation, proof, insight, or argument; the people have rejected their Lord, and the awaited punishment is not with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قل إني على بينة بيان وبرهان وبصيرة وحجة من ربي وكذبتم به أي بربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment belongs only to God, who recounts the truth; the readings with ṣād mean ‘says the truth,’ while the others with ḍād mean ‘judges by truth.’
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز، وعاصم يقص الحق بالصاد المشددة أي يقول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ḍād reading means that God judges truly, supported by ‘the best of deciders’; yāʾ is omitted for ease and al-haqq describes the judgment.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بالضاد أي يحكم بالحق دليله قوله وهو خير الفاصلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet possessed the punishment they demanded, the dispute would end in their destruction; God knows the wrongdoers best.
rows.anchor: لقضي الأمر بيني وبينكم أي فرغ من العذاب وأهلكتم والله أعلم بالظالمين

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says alif-lam-mim-sad is an oath sworn by God.
rows.anchor: المص قسم أقسم الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: ʿAta regards the letters as God’s praise of Himself.
rows.anchor: هو من ثناء الله سبحانه على نفسه

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas treats the initials as a name of God.
rows.anchor: اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو الضحى عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas glosses them as ‘I am God; I distinguish.’
rows.anchor: أنا الله أفصل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the initials are a name for the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: اسم من أسماء القرآن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says these are opening letters with which God began His Book.
rows.anchor: فواتح افتتح الله بها كتابه

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the opening letters are names of God which become a name when joined.
rows.anchor: فواتح السور من أسماء الله تعالى إذا وصلها كانت اسما

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq reads the letters as ‘I am God, the truthful.’
rows.anchor: أنا الله الصادق

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reads them as ‘I am God, most truthful.’
rows.anchor: أنا الله أصدق

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb assigns each initial a divine-name opening, including alif for Ahad and al-lam for Latif, and names beginning with mim and sad.
rows.anchor: إلا أن افتتاح اسمه أحد أول آخر، واللام افتتاح اسمه لطيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say the initials mean ‘Did We not expand your breast?’, are disjoint alphabetic letters, abjad numerals, letters of the greatest name, or letters containing many meanings through which God created as He willed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي حروف هجاء مقطعة، وقيل: هي حساب الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters may be parsed as a subject with Kitab as its predicate, meaning they are letters of the revealed Book; other parses front or defer the wording.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال: (المص) حروف كتاب أنزل إليك

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya glosses ḥaraj as constriction.
rows.anchor: حرج منه قال أبو العالية: ضيق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses ḥaraj as distress or aversion.
rows.anchor: ضيق، وقال مجاهد: تنك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses ḥaraj as sin.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تنك، وقال الضحاك: إثم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the Prophet must have no doubt that the Qurʾan is from God.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: فلا يكن في قلبك شك في القرآن. إنه من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the Prophet should not be burdened by warning and conveying the message; dhikra is an admonition to believers and parses as a nominative dependent on the Book.
rows.anchor: لا أطبق قلبك بإنذار من أرسلتك بإنذاره وإبلاغ من أمرتك بإبلاغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weighing deeds tests faith in worldly life, marks the saved and doomed in the next, shows people their recompense, and establishes the proof against them.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: امتحان الله تعالى عباده بالإيمان به في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing is comparable to the record that speaks with truth and sets out people’s deeds, despite God already knowing them.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق الآية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the heavy balance-pan with a person’s good deeds.
rows.anchor: ثقلت موازينه قال مجاهد: حسناته فأولئك هم المفلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about wronging God’s signs means that they deny them.
rows.anchor: إلى قوله تعالى يظلمون يجحدون

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Gabriel weighs people’s deeds; wrongdoers’ good deeds transfer to victims, or victims’ sins are loaded onto them, leaving them burdened like mountains.
rows.anchor: ليس ثم ذهب ولا فضة وإن كان للظالم حسنات أخذ من حسناته فيرد على المظلوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a balance with tongue and two pans: a believer’s beautiful deeds outweigh sins and lead to Paradise, while a disbeliever’s ugly deeds are light and fall into Hell.
rows.anchor: توزن الحسنات والسيئات في ميزان لسان وكفتان فأما المؤمن فيؤتي بعمله في أحسن صورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since deeds are accidents, the weighed objects are written records containing people’s deeds.
rows.anchor: وإنما توزن الأعمال التي فيها أعمال العباد مكتوبة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: A man’s ninety-nine enormous sin-records are outweighed by a tiny card bearing the testimony that there is no deity but God and Muhammad is His messenger.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بالرجل يوم القيامة إلى الميزان ثم خرج له تسعة وتسعون سجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing is linked to the promise that just balances will be set up for the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية قوله ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural mawazin may be a plural form with singular meaning, like plural terms in the cited verse and al-Aʿsha’s poetry.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون [أعظم] جميعا ومعناه واحد كقوله الذين قال لهم الناس

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s line uses plural ‘breasts’ and ‘forearms’ while intending one of each.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعشى: ووجه نقي اللون صاف يزينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take the plural as the deeds being weighed, or as one great balance with a balance for each servant.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به الأعمال الموزونة. وقيل: الأصل ميزان عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural can refer to the whole balance assembly: its two pans, beam, and tongue, which must come together for weighing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جمعه لأن الميزان ما اشتمل على الكفتين والشاهدين واللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A moral interpretation calls reason the balance distinguishing truth from falsehood, knowledge the balance distinguishing lawful from unlawful, and sound will the balance distinguishing felicity from misery.
rows.anchor: ميزان يفرق به بين الحق والباطل وهو العقل، وميزان يفرق بين الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God established and settled people in the earth and gave them livelihoods in food and drink for their lifetimes; little thanks is given for these gifts.
rows.anchor: ملكناكم في الأرض ووطأنا لكم وجعلناها لكم قرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿayish means the things by which people live; its yāʾ belongs to the root, so it is not written with hamza.
rows.anchor: والمعايش جمع المعيشة الياء من الأصل فلذلك لا تهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Nafiʿ read khalisa in the nominative, meaning ‘purely for them’; the other readers use the accusative because the preceding sentence is complete.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس وقتادة ونافع: خالصة بالرفع يعنون قل هي خالصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fawahish are explained as naked circumambulation: men did so openly by day and women secretly at night; another view says adultery and a further term.
rows.anchor: يعني الطواف عراة ما ظهر منها طواف الرجال بالنهار وما بطن طواف النساء بالليل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says God loves praise, is jealous, and loves to excuse; therefore He praises Himself, forbids indecencies, and sent Scripture and messengers.
rows.anchor: ليس أحد أحب إليه من المدح من الله سبحانه من أجل ذلك مدح نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithm means sin and disobedience; al-Hasan instead says it means wine, as the two cited lines use it for an intoxicant that destroys reason.
rows.anchor: الإثم يعني الذنب والمعصية. وقال الحسن: الإثم الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-baghy means wrongdoing without right; God also forbids associating partners without proof and speaking about Him without knowledge, including invented food and clothing prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والبغي وهو الظلم بغير الحق وأن تشركوا بالله ما لم ينزل به سلطانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community has a fixed term, also interpreted as the time punishment arrives; once it ends, people can neither delay nor hasten it.
rows.anchor: وقت حلول العقاب وأول العذاب. فإذا جاء أجلهم

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin reads the word as the plural ‘their appointed times.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن سيرين آجالهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the address to the children of Adam forbids associating partners with God and that the messenger meant is Muhammad alone.
rows.anchor: وبالرسل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny God’s signs and act arrogantly against them are the people of the Fire, where they remain forever.
rows.anchor: والذين كذبوا بآياتنا واستكبروا عنها عن الإيمان بمحمد والقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering separates unbelievers from believers, placing believers in gardens and unbelievers in the Fire.
rows.anchor: فيدخل الله المؤمن الجنان والكافر النيران

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the evil and good distinguished are evil and righteous deeds, rewarded with Hell and Paradise respectively.
rows.anchor: يعني العمل الخبيث من العمل الطيب الصالح فيثيب على الأعمال الصالحة الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufans, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Aʿmash, and ʿIsa read the verb with shadda, a reading preferred by Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة والحسن وقتادة والأعمش وعيسى: ليميز الله بالتشديد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the contrast as good spending for God versus evil spending for Satan, with the latter piled into Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني الإنفاق الطيب في سبيل الله من الإنفاق الخبيث في سبيل الشيطان

rows.speaker: مرة الهمداني
rows.claim: Murra al-Hamdani says prior divine knowledge distinguished believers created good from unbelievers created evil; obedience or refusal manifests this distinction.
rows.anchor: يميز المؤمن في علمه السابق الذي خلقه حين خلقه طيبا من الخبيث الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rakama means piling things densely like a gathered cloud; the singular predicate first follows khabith, then the plural ‘those’ returns to the earlier people who spent.
rows.anchor: حتى يصيره مثل السحاب الركام وهو المجتمع الكثيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers are those whose bargain failed: they bought punishment in the next life with their wealth.
rows.anchor: الذين غنيت صفقتهم وخسرت تجارتهم لأنهم اشتروا بأموالهم عذاب الله في الآخرة

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Muhammad says ‘if they desist’ means desist from shirk; if they return to fighting, the earlier pattern of prophetic victory and unbeliever destruction, as at Badr, applies.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد: يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من عملهم قبل الإسلام

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh hopes that pure monotheism which erases earlier unbelief can also erase later sins.
rows.anchor: إني لأرجو أن توحيدا لم يعجز عن هدم ما قبله من كفر

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد أحمد بن محمد الزيدي
rows.claim: A poem says a person who admits and abandons wrongdoing deserves pardon, citing God’s promise to forgive those who desist.
rows.anchor: أبو سعيد أحمد بن محمد الزيدي: يستوجب العفو الفتى إذا اعترف

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya interprets fitna as shirk.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: بلاء، وقال الربيع

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says fighting continues until believers are no longer persecuted for their religion and pure monotheism belongs wholly to God.
rows.anchor: حتى لا يفتن مؤمن عن دينه ويكون الدين التوحيد خالصا كله لله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the endpoint is that people say ‘there is no god but God,’ the call to which the Prophet fought and invited.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: حتى يقال: لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that all obedience and worship should be exclusive to God.
rows.anchor: حتى تكون الطاعة والعبادة لله خالصة دون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents stop disbelief and fighting, God sees their deeds; if they turn back, God is their protector, helper, and excellent ally.
rows.anchor: فإن انتهوا عن الكفر والقتال فإن الله بما يعملون بصير

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes take God’s turning toward the Prophet as His permission for hypocrites to stay behind.
rows.anchor: بإذنه للمنافقين في التخلف عنهم

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Grammarians call the clause an opening connective: the Prophet’s repentance is not of the same kind as the others’ repentance, like the phrasing about God and His Messenger receiving the fifth.
rows.anchor: هو مفتاح كلام ما كان هو صنف توبتهم ذكر معهم

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir says the ‘hour of hardship’ meant hardship in mounts, provisions, and water.
rows.anchor: قال جابر: عسرة الظهر وعسرة الزاد وعسرة الماء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan describes the campaign’s deprivation: shared mounts, rotten dates and barley, rancid fat, and passing a date around while sharing water.
rows.anchor: كان الناس من المسلمين يخرجون على بعير يعقبونه بينهم يركب الرجل ساعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar recounts severe thirst in the heat of Tabuk; at Abu Bakr’s urging the Prophet prayed, a cloud rained over the army, and no farther.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر: خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم [إلى قيض شديد]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three left behind were those who failed to join Tabuk; another view says their judgment was deferred after Abu Lubaba and his companions’ repentance.
rows.anchor: يعني تاب على الثلاثة الذين تخلفوا عن غزوة تبوك فلم يخرجوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about hearts almost turning is explained as near deviation because of the severe trial; readers differ between tāʾ and yāʾ, with al-Aʿmash intending a delayed subject.
rows.anchor: تميل قلوب فريق منهم لعظم البلاء، وقرأ العامة: تزاغ، بالتاء

rows.speaker: عكرمة وحميد
rows.claim: They read khullifu with fatḥa and light consonants, meaning that the three came after the Prophet; Jaʿfar al-Sadiq reads khalafu and al-Aʿmash reads al-mukhallafin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة وحميد: خلفوا بفتح الخاء واللام والتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three left behind were Kaʿb ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayya, all from the Ansar.
rows.anchor: وهم كعب بن مالك الشاعر ومرارة بن الربيع وهلال بن أمية كلهم من الأنصار

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb says he never missed a campaign except Badr and Tabuk; the Prophet did not censure Badr absentees because the expedition sought a caravan and the battle happened unexpectedly.
rows.anchor: لم أتخلف عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة غزاها حتى كانت غزوة تبوك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb says he valued the pledge of al-ʿAqaba more than having been present at Badr.
rows.anchor: وما أحب أني كنت شهدتها مكان بيعتي ليلة العقبة

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the Prophet usually concealed his military destination, but for Tabuk he wanted people to prepare openly because of the distance and hardship.
rows.anchor: وكان قل ما أراد غزوة إلا [ورى غيرها] وكان يقول: الحرب خدعة

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Though well equipped with two mounts and inclined to campaign, Kaʿb delayed during the pleasant shade and ripe fruit until the army had left.
rows.anchor: وأنا أيسر ما كنت قد جهزت راحلتين، وأنا أقدر شيء في نفسي الجهاد

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: In the city Kaʿb saw no other absentees except people suspected of hypocrisy or those excused for weakness; roughly eighty others had stayed behind.
rows.anchor: لا أرى أحدا تخلف إلا رجلا مغموصا عليه في النفاق أو رجلا ممن عذر الله

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet did not ask about Kaʿb until reaching Tabuk, where he asked what had happened to him.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكرني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى بلغ تبوك فقال

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: When someone alleged that Kaʿb was vainly admiring his clothes and body, Muʿadh defended him, saying they knew nothing but good of him.
rows.anchor: بئس ما قلت والله يا نبي الله ما نعلم إلا خيرا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Seeing a man approach through the mirage, the Prophet recognized him as Abu Khaythama, who had given a measure of dates and been mocked by hypocrites.
rows.anchor: كن أبا خيثمة الأنصاري وهو الذي تصدق بصاع التمر فلمزه المنافقون

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: On the return to Medina, Kaʿb weighed whether to escape the Prophet’s anger with a pretext, then chose truth as the only way to be saved.
rows.anchor: وعرفت أن لا أنجو إلا بالصدق

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb admits he had no excuse and had never been more able or better equipped than when he stayed behind.
rows.anchor: قلت: والله لو كنت بين يدي أجد من الناس غيرك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet accepts Kaʿb’s confession as truthful and leaves his case to God’s judgment.
rows.anchor: أما هذا فقد صدقكم الحديث قم حتى يقضي الله فيك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb’s relatives urged him to offer an excuse like the others, but after learning Hilal ibn Umayya and Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ also told the truth, he refused to lie.
rows.anchor: هلال بن أمية الواقفي وأبو مرارة بن ربيعة العامري

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet ordered people not to speak to the three truthful absentees, beginning a prolonged social boycott.
rows.anchor: قال: ونهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الناس عن كلامنا

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the people and even familiar walls and land seemed changed; he went to the market and mosque, but the Prophet would not meet his gaze.
rows.anchor: وتنكرت لنا الحيطان حتى ما هي الحيطان التي نعرف وتنكرت لنا الأرض

rows.speaker: أبو قتادة
rows.claim: Abu Qatada would not confirm Kaʿb’s love for God and His Messenger, replying that God and His Messenger know best.
rows.anchor: فقال: الله ورسوله أعلم

rows.speaker: ملك غسان
rows.claim: The king of Ghassan invited Kaʿb to leave the Prophet’s community for a place where he would be supported; Kaʿb burned the letter as a trial.
rows.anchor: فقلت: هذا من البلاء والشرف فسجرت التنور فأحرقته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Kaʿb to avoid his wife without divorcing her; he gave the same order regarding the wives of the other two, while allowing Hilal’s wife to serve him without intimacy.
rows.anchor: «اعتزل امرأتك» فقلت: أطلقها. قال: «لا ولكن لا تقربها»
